result.Method of Attack: Typosquatting popular Lodash library to trick developers; Contains base64-obfuscated code that launches a bundled 'dataset.db' file which is a tainted Windows AnyDesk executable; Creates a Google directory in APPDATA, copies AnyDesk executable renamed as Chrome.exe, and executes it to establish remote access
result.Attack Vector: Malicious npm package installation via typosquatting
result.Indicators of Compromise: Package names similar to Lodash but with version 4.17.24 (vs Lodash 4.17.21); Base64-obfuscated index.js code; Bundled 'dataset.db' file which is actually a Windows EXE (AnyDesk.exe); Execution of Chrome.exe renamed AnyDesk binary in APPDATA\Google directory; Code signing certificate from 'philandro Software GmbH' dated April 7, 2020; Connections to domain 'api.playanext.com'; Sonatype tracking ID sonatype-2024-011383; References in legitimate package READMEs (e.g., restrict-imports-loader) lending false credibility
